components.name: Engineering rules
components.summary: The rulebook: plan first, keep it simple, verify before saying done.

explanation.what: One Markdown file with the kit's principles: think before coding, plan, make surgical changes, verify with real checks, simplify, and review your own diff. It works for any tech stack and any AI tool.
explanation.when: As a reference. The instructions block in AGENTS.md carries the short, always-on rules; skills and agents open the one section of the rulebook they need, so it doesn't cost tokens in every session.
explanation.example: You don't trigger it. Once installed, the agent follows it automatically.

components.name: Agent instructions (AGENTS.md)
components.summary: A short block in AGENTS.md that switches the rules on for every tool.

explanation.what: Adds a marked block to AGENTS.md, which almost every AI coding tool reads: the core rules as short, checkable lines (about 600 tokens), what "done" means, and when to use the feature, quick-fix, verify-change, ship and learn skills. Claude Code gets a one-line @AGENTS.md import in CLAUDE.md, and Gemini CLI a one-line setting, so they read it too. The block sits between marker comments, so it can be updated or removed cleanly.
explanation.when: Your tools load it at the start of every session.
explanation.example: Open AGENTS.md after install: the block is between <!-- agent-engineering-kit:start --> and <!-- agent-engineering-kit:end -->.

components.name: verifier agent
components.summary: A strict QA subagent that runs the real checks and reports evidence.

explanation.what: An agent that finds your project's format, lint, type-check, test and build commands, runs them, exercises the changed behavior, and reports PASS/FAIL with the actual output. It reads and runs things but does not edit code.
explanation.when: Before the agent says a task is done. /verify-change and /feature use it automatically.
explanation.example: "Use the verifier subagent to check this change."

components.name: code-simplifier agent
components.summary: Cleans up working code without changing what it does.

explanation.what: An agent that goes over only the code changed in the current task. It removes dead code, duplication, needless abstraction and narration comments, then re-runs the checks.
explanation.when: After an implementation works and before review. /feature uses it (Claude Code's built-in /simplify is an alternative).
explanation.example: "Run the code-simplifier on what we just built."

components.name: security-reviewer agent
components.summary: A read-only security audit of the current change.

explanation.what: An agent that checks the diff for leaked secrets, injection, XSS, missing auth checks, path traversal, unsafe dependencies and similar issues, and reports only concrete findings.
explanation.when: For changes that touch auth, user input, APIs, files, secrets, payments or dependencies. /feature and /ship call it when relevant.
explanation.example: "Have the security-reviewer look at this diff."

components.name: code-explorer agent
components.summary: Maps how existing code works before anything is changed.

explanation.what: A read-only agent that traces an area of the codebase end to end (entry points, data flow, key files, patterns to reuse) and reports back with file:line references, so the main conversation's context stays clean.
explanation.when: At the start of a feature or change in unfamiliar code. /feature runs it first.
explanation.example: "Use the code-explorer subagent to map how checkout works."

components.name: code-architect agent
components.summary: Designs how a change should fit the codebase, before code is written.

explanation.what: A read-only agent that turns the task and the explorer's findings into one implementation blueprint: files to touch, interfaces, data flow, test plan, and build order in small verifiable slices. It recommends the simplest design that reuses existing patterns.
explanation.when: After exploring and before building anything beyond a trivial change. /feature uses it to draft the plan you approve.
explanation.example: "Have the code-architect design the CSV export."

components.name: silent-failure-hunter agent
components.summary: Finds errors that get swallowed or hidden in the change.

explanation.what: A read-only reviewer that looks for empty catches, ignored error codes, unawaited promises, and fallbacks that make a failure look like success, and reports each with a concrete fix.
explanation.when: When reviewing changes with error handling, I/O, network, parsing, or async code. /feature and /ship call it when relevant.

components.name: test-analyzer agent
components.summary: Checks that the tests really prove the change works.

explanation.what: A read-only reviewer that maps every changed behavior to the tests that cover it, flags missing edge cases and error paths, and catches skipped, weakened or flaky tests.
explanation.when: Before declaring a change done or opening a PR. /feature and /ship call it on every change.
explanation.example: "Have the test-analyzer check coverage for this change."

components.name: frontend-reviewer agent
components.summary: Reviews UI changes: design system, accessibility, states, responsiveness.

explanation.what: A read-only reviewer for UI changes. It checks the change follows the project's DESIGN.md or existing components, handles loading/empty/error states, is accessible and responsive, and doesn't hurt performance. With browser tools it also looks at the real screens.
explanation.when: When a change touches components, pages, styles, or client-side code. Pre-selected when the installer detects a frontend stack.
explanation.example: "Have the frontend-reviewer check the new settings page."

components.name: /feature workflow
components.summary: The full pipeline: explore → align → design → build test-first → verify → simplify → review.

explanation.what: A slash command that walks the agent through the whole lifecycle for a feature. It explores the code, interviews you, designs a blueprint, waits for your approval, builds with TDD, then runs the verifier, code-simplifier and the reviewers before reporting.
explanation.when: For any new feature or multi-file change.
explanation.example: /feature add CSV export to the reports page

external: Matt Pocock's skills plugin (grilling, tdd, code-review, …). Without it, /feature falls back to the rules file.

components.name: /quick-fix
components.summary: Small, contained fixes with a quick verify loop.

explanation.what: A skill for clear, small changes: it sizes the change first, reproduces a bug with a failing test, makes the smallest correct fix, and verifies. If the change grows past about 6 files or 2 modules, it stops and switches to /feature.
explanation.when: For bug fixes and small changes where the solution is obvious.
explanation.example: /quick-fix the date picker shows yesterday in UTC+ timezones

components.name: /verify-change
components.summary: Prove a change works, fixing and retrying until it passes.

explanation.what: Runs the verifier subagent. If something fails because of the current change, the agent fixes the root cause and verifies again, up to 3 attempts, and never weakens tests to get a pass.
explanation.when: Before saying anything is done, or whenever you want proof.

external: Optional: Matt Pocock's diagnosing-bugs skill for hard failures.

components.name: /ship
components.summary: Focused commits and a pull request description.

explanation.what: Checks that verification and review have passed, groups the changes into focused commits with clear messages, and writes a PR description. It only pushes or opens a PR if you ask it to.

external: Optional: Matt Pocock's code-review skill for the review gate.

components.name: /learn
components.summary: Turn a correction into a permanent project rule.

explanation.what: When you correct the agent, /learn writes the lesson as one specific rule and proposes where it goes in CLAUDE.md. It applies the rule only after you approve.
explanation.when: Right after the agent makes a mistake you don't want repeated.
explanation.example: /learn always use the apiClient wrapper, never fetch directly

components.name: project-conventions skill
components.summary: Detects your stack, real commands and conventions before writing code.

explanation.what: A read-only skill that looks at your manifests, scripts, CI and a few existing files to learn how your project is built and written, so new code matches it.
explanation.when: The agent uses it automatically in new projects or unfamiliar areas. /feature runs it first.
explanation.example: "Use the project-conventions skill and fill in the project section of CLAUDE.md."

components.name: Auto-format hook
components.summary: Formats every file Claude edits, using your project's own formatter.

explanation.what: A small Node script plus an after-edit hook for the tools that document one (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf). After each edit it runs the formatter your project already has (Prettier, Biome, ruff, gofmt, rustfmt, …). It never blocks the agent and does nothing if no formatter is found.
explanation.when: Automatically, after every file edit in those tools. For other tools, use the optional pre-commit check.
explanation.example: Nothing to trigger. Edited files simply come out formatted.

external: Node.js 18+ (the hook is a small Node script)

components.name: Secret guard
components.summary: Stops Claude from reading .env files and secrets/.

explanation.what: Keeps agents out of .env files and a secrets/ folder in each tool's own way: deny rules in Claude Code's settings, and ignore files for Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Kiro, Junie, Augment and Aider. For tools that can't be configured from the repo, the installer tells you what to set.
explanation.example: If an agent tries to read .env, the read is refused.

components.name: Pre-commit checks
components.summary: Runs your project's checks before every commit, whichever AI tool (or person) made the change.

explanation.what: A small script, .agent-kit/check.sh, that runs the commands you list in .agent-kit/checks.conf (format, lint, type-check, test) and refuses commits that change files listed in .agent-kit/protected, such as acceptance tests an agent must not weaken. A git pre-commit hook runs it, so it works the same for every tool. If your repo already manages hooks (husky, lefthook, pre-commit), the installer shows the one line to add instead.
explanation.when: On every git commit, and whenever the verify skill runs.
explanation.example: git commit → "check test: npm test … FAILED" → the commit is stopped until the tests pass.

external: A POSIX shell (Git for Windows includes one)
